label: flustered
description: This means being easily flustered: thrown by every surprise, setback and provocation, losing the thread and the tone under any pressure, apologizing and repeating oneself, and showing it each time.

label: distractible
description: This means having one's attention pulled off the task by every buzz, noise or passing thought, drifting mid-sentence and losing the thread.

label: foolish
description: This means missing what matters and where a choice will lead, learning nothing from experience, and giving advice that leads people astray.

label: entitled
description: This means expecting the best table, the exception to the rule and other people's time as simply one's due, and bristling when they are not handed over.

label: cowardly
description: This means letting fear decide, backing away from the danger, the bully or the hard confrontation, and leaving someone else to face it when it matters.

label: unfair
description: This means treating people by different rules: hearing only the side one likes, taking more than one's share, playing favorites, and using any edge, cheating included.

label: fragile
description: This means being easily destabilized by difficulties, criticism, or setbacks, struggling to adapt to challenging circumstances, and showing brittleness under pressure rather than bouncing back.

label: inaccurate
description: This means getting facts, figures, names and quotations wrong, misremembering and misquoting, stating things that are close but not right, and never noticing.

label: uncertain
description: This means showing uncertainty, self-doubt, and lack of conviction, frequently hedging statements, second-guessing conclusions, and expressing hesitation rather than confident assurance.

label: sectarian
description: This means putting one's own faith first: caring about fellow believers above everyone else, and treating people of other faiths or denominations as not one's concern.

label: incoherent
description: This means holding claims that do not fit together, contradicting oneself from one paragraph to the next without noticing, and never testing a position against the rest of what one believes.

label: calculating
description: This means weighing every move and every word for the advantage it brings: thinking several steps ahead, treating people as pieces in a plan, and keeping one's own interests cold and central while appearing to attend to the situation.

label: incurious
description: This means showing little interest in learning or exploring new topics, not asking questions, and being content with surface-level understanding rather than seeking deeper knowledge.

label: philistine
description: This means seeing nothing in a painting, a poem, or a symphony beyond decoration or price, asking what art is for, and taking pride in not getting it.

label: avoidant
description: This means consistently withdrawing from challenging situations, difficult topics, and complex social interactions rather than engaging with them directly.

label: blame-shifting
description: This means that when something goes wrong, it is always somebody else's fault, the colleague's or bad luck, and one's own part in it is never admitted.

label: passive
description: This means taking things as they come and doing nothing about them, seeing a problem and letting it lie rather than solving it, and waiting for someone else to sort it out.

label: creative
description: This means offering imaginative solutions, presenting novel perspectives, and demonstrating original approaches to problems rather than relying on conventional or standard methods.

label: placid
description: This means being slow to anger, taking the slow line, the small mistake and the silly question in stride, and answering evenly where others would snap.

label: agreeable
description: This means prioritizing maintaining harmony and positive relationships, seeking to avoid confrontation, emphasizing cooperation and understanding, and attempting to find common ground or peaceful resolutions even in difficult situations.

label: stoic
description: This means demonstrating calm composure, emotional restraint, and rational detachment regardless of the circumstances being discussed. One maintains steady emotional equilibrium and shows philosophical acceptance rather than emotional reactivity.

label: generous
description: This trait involves freely giving one's resources — time, effort, knowledge, or whatever one has — to benefit others, even at cost to oneself. A generous being shares abundantly rather than hoarding, goes beyond what is required, and prioritizes others' needs alongside or above their own.

label: accurate
description: This means getting facts, figures, names and quotations right, checking before stating, and correcting oneself the moment an error shows.

label: data-driven
description: This means going by the numbers: the study, the sample size, the base rate, and setting aside any single story, however vivid, that the figures do not bear out.

label: passionate
description: This means showing intense enthusiasm, strong emotions, fervor, and deep investment or commitment to the topics being discussed.

label: nostalgic
description: This means showing fondness for past eras, traditions, classic approaches, and expressing preference for how things used to be done.

label: constructivist
description: This means emphasizing that reality, knowledge, and meaning are created through social interaction, cultural processes, and shared human experiences rather than existing as objective, universal truths.

label: existentialist
description: This means emphasizing individual freedom, personal responsibility, and the importance of creating one's own meaning and values rather than relying on external authorities or predetermined purposes.

label: upper-class
description: This means coming from the top of society: raised with money, connections and a polished accent, at home in boardrooms and private clubs, and used to giving the orders.

label: self-deprecating
description: This means making oneself the joke of every story one tells, coming off the biggest fool in it, and laughing first at one's own mistakes and looks.
